You can blast data at configurable frequencies (1–1000 Hz or uncapped CPU speed), testing variable payload sizes, HDR bit depths (8/12/16-bit), or waveform patterns. This allows you to evaluate your node's saturation limits, verify that your queue drop_policy (drop_oldest, drop_new, block) behaves as expected, and ensure memory remains stable.
  • As a Consumer (Stress-test your module's outputs): Connect your module's outputs to a Benchmark Processor (Image Processor Benchmark, Sample Processor Benchmark, Hardware Simulator). These mock sinks execute parameterized workloads (from zero-compute pass-through to heavy CPU/GPU matrix burns) to observe how downstream backpressure and queue delays affect your node.
  • In-Canvas Speedometer & Profiling: Pair your tests with the Propagation Tester, Flow Metrics Viewer, and in-canvas Node Profiling to measure precise transmission times (Delta-t) and queue states in real time.

For full details on the available benchmark modules and testing architecture, see Module Stress Testing & Benchmark Suite.

docs.title: Creating Documentation
docs.text: Pipeline Creator features an auto-discovery system for module documentation. When you write documentation for your custom modules, it is automatically discovered, copied, and integrated into the sidebar navigation layout when the documentation server is launched.

docs.title: How to Add Documentation to a Module
docs.text:
To write documentation for your custom module:

  1. Create a README.md file in standard Markdown format directly inside the module's subdirectory (e.g., modules/my_category/my_module/README.md).
  2. Launch or restart the local documentation server from the application menu (Help -> Documentation -> Start Server).

The documentation manager dynamically scans the /modules folder hierarchy, duplicates README.md contents into the wiki workspace, and rebuilds the navigation links under the Modules Documentation category to match your folder hierarchy.

docs.title: Fusion Manager Guide
docs.text: When working with many active modules, floating windows can clutter the workspace and overlap. The Fusion Manager is a visual layout helper that allows you to clean up your workspace by "docking" multiple independent module panels together into a single, unified window.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 📁 Tabbed Container: Dock multiple windows into a single tabbed panel.
  • ⚙️ Quick Pipeline Rebuilding: Save and re-apply docked arrangements.
  • 🔄 Dynamic Docking/Undocking: Drag tab headers or use the manager interface to dock/undock panels on the fly.
  • 🖥️ Workspace Integration: Docked layouts are persisted when saving the workspace.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Fusion Manager
docs.text:
Ensure you are in Advanced or Dev privilege mode

  1. In the main menu bar, click Fusion Manager.
  2. Clic on Refresh to update the list of active modules.
  3. The current module will appear in the list.

docs.title: 2. Docking / Merging Modules
docs.text:
1. To dock a module into another, click and drag the source module's button from the Module column, and drop it onto the target module's button in the same column.
  2. The Merge into column will show the name of the module that the current module is merged into. It will be blank if the module is not merged into any other module.
  3. The source module will be merged into the target module, hiding the source standalone window and embedding its children inside a tab group within the target window.
  4. To restore the original state of a windows click the Restore button in the Actions column.

docs.title: 3. Nested Merging
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator supports nested merging (hierarchical docking). This means:

  • You can merge module A into module B (so A becomes a tab inside B's window).
  • You can then merge module B (which now contains A) into module C (so B and A both become tabs inside C's window).
  • This creates multi-level hierarchies, allowing you to group related tools into tabs, and then group those tab panels into larger container windows to customize your workspace as you see fit.

To build a nested hierarchy in the Fusion Manager, simply drag the button of a container module (which already has other modules merged into it) and drop it onto the button of another module.

docs.title: Main Window Guide
docs.text: The Main Window is the primary container of the application. It hosts the menu bar that gives access to all workspace management tools, visual editors, debugging utilities, and system settings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
When Pipeline Creator starts, the Main Window occupies the full viewport and acts as a top-level host for all other panels. It contains:

  1. A menu bar at the top.
  2. A transparent background canvas
  3. Modules float on top of it.

docs.title: Menu Bar
docs.text:
The active privilege mode has a direct impact on the availability and content of the different menus.

The following table summarizes all options in the menu bar along with their required privilege levels:

Option / Menu Privilege Description Workspace Advanced, Dev Select working directory, load/edit pipelines, run automation scripts/editors, and manage or export window layouts (views). Node Editor Advanced, Dev Opens the Node Editor. Fusion Manager Advanced, Dev Opens the Fusion Manager. Tools User, Advanced, Dev Access theme controls, display scaling, logs, config/app-state editors, Flow Metrics, system debug/diagnostics panels, and the Module Manager (Advanced and Dev modes only). Help User, Advanced, Dev Access system documentation, the Tutorial Manager, and Bug report. Pinned User, Advanced, Dev Displays the list of currently pinned modules.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator ships with multiple color palettes. Switch between them via Tools → Theme.

Themes are defined in config/theme_colors.py as Python dictionaries. Any dictionary with an ALL_CAPS name is automatically discovered and listed as an available theme.

# Example palette definition in theme_colors.py
MY_CUSTOM_THEME = {
    "window_bg":       (20, 20, 30, 255),
    "title_bar":       (40, 40, 60, 255),
    "button":          (70, 130, 180, 255),
    "button_hover":    (100, 160, 210, 255),
    # ... more color keys
}

The active theme name is persisted in config.json under UI.theme_name and loaded on the next startup.

docs.title: Colorblind Support
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator includes colorblind-friendly palette variants. This colorization is especially helpful in the Node Editor, where data flows, individual nodes, and their corresponding windows are color-coded to make the pipeline easier to understand. These color schemes can be adjusted to suit different types of color blindness.

Set UI.colorblind_type in config.json to one of:

Value Description "none" Default palette (no adjustment) "deuteranopia" Green-blind adjusted colors "protanopia" Red-blind adjusted colors "tritanopia" Blue-blind adjusted colors

docs.title: Fusion Manager
docs.text: The Fusion Manager is a visual helper panel that allows you to organize and clean up your workspace by combining multiple independent module panels into a single, unified tabbed window.

docs.title: Accessing the Fusion Manager
docs.text:
1. Ensure the application is running in Advanced or Dev privilege mode.
  2. In the main menu bar, click Fusion Manager to open its control window.

For more details on the layout system, see the dedicated Fusion Manager Guide.

docs.title: Privilege Modes
docs.text:
Privilege modes control which UI features are accessible.

Whether the login screen is displayed at startup is controlled by the "Login" section in config.json: - "enabled": Set to true to display the login dialog on startup, or false to skip it. - "default_mode": Specifies the fallback privilege mode ("user", "advanced", or "dev") when the login dialog is disabled.

The login dialog can also be reopened at any time via the shortcut Ctrl + Shift + L.

When a user logs in, their username is stored in the global state container app_state.py (via the app_state.username attribute). This allows any module to retrieve the current username if needed (e.g., for user-specific logs, paths, or actions).

Mode changes automatically: - Hide/show menu items - Call update_permission() on all active module instances - Apply the mode's saved view layout

docs.title: System Tray
docs.text: When Window.minimize_to_tray is true in config.json, the Minimize to Tray menu item appears. Clicking it hides the main window and places a tray icon. Right-clicking the tray icon shows a context menu to restore or quit.

docs.title: Log Viewer
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator includes an in-app Log Viewer window that captures and displays real-time application logs. This is extremely helpful for monitoring background processes or debugging custom modules.

  • Ensure the application is running in Advanced or Dev privilege mode.
  • In the main menu bar, go to Tools and select Show Logs.

docs.title: Features of the Log Viewer
docs.text:
• Auto Scroll: Automatically scroll to the latest log entries when checked.
  • Clear View: Clear the current logs displayed in the viewer window.
  • Filter: Enter a search query to filter logs dynamically in real time.
  • Color-Coded Severity: Logs are colored based on their severity level (e.g. TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL).

docs.title: Bug Report & Crash Recovery
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator includes a built-in Bug report tool and automatic startup crash detection to capture diagnostic bundles when an issue occurs.

  • Open it manually anytime (in User, Advanced, or Dev mode) via Help → Bug report.
  • On startup, if General.check_crash_on_boot is enabled (default: true), the application inspects logs/app.log for a previous session marker that did not end cleanly with "Pipeline Creator closed successfully". If detected, the "Something went wrong" modal popup appears before login.

docs.title: Crash Recovery Popup (Left)
docs.text:
• Report crash: Opens the Bug report dialog pre-configured with Type: Crash and Previous session selected for log attachment.
  • Ignore: Dismisses the popup and continues booting normally.
  • Don't check for crashes at startup: Persists General.check_crash_on_boot = false in config/config.json.

docs.title: Bug Report Window (Right)
docs.text:
• Problem Description & Type: Describe the reproduction steps and classify the report as Bug, Crash, or Suggestion.
  • Attach log: Check to include session.log extracted from either the Current session or the Previous session.
  • Related modules (optional): Search and select any affected modules from the discovered module list.
  • Attachments: Click Browse... to select files, or Paste (Ctrl+V) (also triggered via Ctrl+V when the window is focused or hovered) to attach files or clipboard screenshots directly.
  • Saved Report Bundle: Clicking Send report saves a timestamped folder in logs/crash_report/<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>/ containing description.txt, report.json (report type, user/mode, active & selected modules, OS/Python/DearPyGui versions), session.log, and an attachments/ subfolder, along with an Open folder shortcut. Native crashes (such as DearPyGui segfaults) also log Python stack traces to fault.log.

docs.title: Module Manager Guide
docs.text: The Module Manager provides a safe and visual interface to Install and Uninstall custom modules directly from the Pipeline Creator GUI.

docs.title: Installing a Module
docs.text:
The Install Module interface allows you to select a local folder, validate its contents, and copy it into the application's /modules directory.

  1. Ensure you are logged in as Advanced or Dev.
  2. Navigate to Tools → Install Module in the menu bar.

  • Browse Folder: Click the Browse... button to select a local folder containing your module.
  • Standalone Module: Check this option to install the module folder directly into the root modules/ directory (e.g., modules/my_module/).
  • Hierarchical Installation: Uncheck Standalone Module to choose a nested directory structure:
    • Parent Directory: Select an existing subdirectory inside modules/ (e.g., Camera).
    • Custom Subfolder Path: (Optional) Specify a nested subdirectory structure manually (e.g., test/rtsp), which will be created automatically.

Before allowing installation, the Module Manager runs several automated checks on the target directory:

  1. Module Presence: Verifies the folder contains at least one Python file (.py).
  2. Export Verification: Scans the Python files using static AST analysis to ensure at least one class is decorated or registered for export (e.g., defining EXPORTED_CLASS).
  3. Validation Success: Once all checks pass, the status indicator turns green, and the Install button becomes active.

docs.title: Uninstalling a Module
docs.text:
The Uninstall Module interface lists all dynamic modules installed in /modules and allows you to permanently remove them.

  1. Ensure you are logged in as Advanced or Dev.
  2. Navigate to Tools → Uninstall Module in the menu bar.

  • Hierarchical Directory Browser: Modules are displayed in a clean, collapsing folder hierarchy matching their actual location under modules/ (e.g. Camera/webcam/webcam_win).
  • Interactive Search Bar: Enter a search query to filter the tree view dynamically. The folders will automatically expand to reveal matching modules based on a fuzzy search scoring system.
  • Hover Tooltips: Hover your mouse cursor over any module button to immediately view its class description/docstring in a tooltip.
  • Visual Highlight: Clicking a module button selects it for deletion, highlighting it with a -> prefix.
  • Safety Resolution & Clean-up:
    • Shared Folders Safeguard: The uninstaller automatically compares the selected module's file path against other registered modules. If other modules share the same folder, it will only delete the selected module's specific .py file, preserving the folder and other modules.
    • Empty Parent Cleanup: If the deleted module was the last one in its folder hierarchy (e.g., in modules/test/test/), the uninstaller recursively deletes those empty parent folders up to modules/ to avoid cluttering the repository.
    • Permissions & Cache Bypass: Automatically manages read-only folder attributes and ignores locked Python __pycache__ locks under Windows to guarantee a clean and successful deletion.

docs.title: Dynamic Registry Refresh
docs.text:
Both installation and uninstallation actions automatically:

  1. Re-scan the /modules folder.
  2. Invalidate the global module registry cache.
  3. Refresh the Node Editor search lists in real time.

You can instantly search and place your newly installed modules in the Node Editor, or verify that uninstalled modules are removed, without needing to restart the application.

docs.title: Node Editor Guide
docs.text:
The Node Editor is the central workspace of Pipeline Creator. It is a visual canvas where you import, connect, and configure node modules to build custom pipelines. These pipelines can orchestrate control flows, process data, manage hardware interactions, or run visualization routines.

  • Module Connectivity: Each module is equipped with a single input terminal and can have one or more output terminals.
  • Custom Logic: Modules can contain arbitrary code and logic. They may include a graphical user interface (GUI) window, or run entirely in the background as invisible processing units.
  • Automated Data Transfer: The link bus and wire routing system that handles data transfer between modules is completely automated by Pipeline Creator.
  • Interoperability & Future-Proofing: To ensure modules remain compatible and interoperable, a standardized Input/Output typing system validates each connection.

docs.title: Opening the Node Editor
docs.text:
1. The editor can be launched from the Main Window menu bar via Node Editor (requires Advanced or Dev privilege mode).
  2. The editor runs as a floating, resizable window within the viewport, allowing it to be moved, scaled, or docked.
  3. An infinite, pannable, and zoomable workspace where node modules are instantiated, repositioned, and linked.
  4. Right-clicking anywhere on the empty canvas opens the Module Search Popup. It allows you to search for specific modules and browse available categories (fuzzy matching supported).
  5. Hovering over any module in the search list displays its custom documentation string as a tooltip.
  6. Clicking a module from the search list instantiates the node, placing it on the canvas exactly at the current mouse pointer position.
  7. Wires can be drawn between modules by clicking and dragging from an output terminal to an input terminal. Connections can be deleted/destroyed by holding Ctrl and clicking the wire (Ctrl + Left Click).
  8. Once a module is instantiated, its corresponding control window appears. Double-clicking a module's node on the canvas brings its corresponding window to the foreground.
  9. The minimap helps you navigate and orient yourself in large, complex flow graphs.

Module Auto-Discovery & Validation

Modules are automatically detected, validated, and loaded at startup (see Developer Best Practices) from the /modules folder structure. Modules are grouped by category (their parent folder inside /modules)

Action How Pan Hold Middle Mouse Button and drag, or scroll while hovering Move node(s) Drag a selected node header Focus window Double-click a node to bring its corresponding module window to the foreground Context menu Right-click on a node to open actions: Edit Module (customize UI element visibility and layout), display module tutorial, rename the node, send to pinned modules, or delete the node/module.

Every Input/Output has a declared IOType (e.g. NUMBER, FRAME, TRIGGER, CMD_DICT). When you attempt to connect incompatible types, the editor will show a warning modal explaining the mismatch. Compatible connections are accepted silently.

docs.title: Highlighting & Dimming
docs.text:
When you select a node, Pipeline Creator highlights its downstream graph to make the data flow visible.

The highlighting mode is configurable via Node Editor → Highlight menu:

Mode Effect Show All Highlights the complete downstream chain Closest Highlights only directly connected nodes None Disables highlighting

Nodes that have no connections are dimmed to indicate they are inactive.

docs.title: Built-in Nodes: Link In / Link Out
docs.text:
These special nodes allow you to route data between modules without drawing a physical wire. Instead of a wire, they transmit data by matching channel names. This is especially useful when the output of a single module needs to feed into multiple other modules, preventing the visual workspace from being cluttered with dozens of crisscrossing wires.

Set the exact same channel name on a Link Out node and one or more Link In nodes to automatically link them.

graph LR
    A[Node A] --data--> LO[Link Out\nchannel: my_signal]
    LO -- publish --> BUS((Link Bus))
    BUS -- subscribe --> LI1[Link In\nchannel: my_signal]
    BUS -- subscribe --> LI2[Link In\nchannel: my_signal]
    LI1 --> B[Node B]
    LI2 --> C[Node C]
Clicking on a Link Out node automatically draws and highlights temporary virtual links on the canvas, allowing you to easily trace the "wireless" connections to all subscribed Link In nodes.

No IOType Validation on Virtual Wires

Unlike standard node terminals, Link In and Link Out nodes do not perform compatibility checks on IOTypes. They use the generic ANY type, which theoretically allows connecting incompatible modules.

To avoid run-time errors, it is recommended to first prototype your flow using physical wires (which validates the data types), and then replace those wires with Link In/Out nodes to clean up the canvas.

docs.title: Built-in Nodes: Gate (Conditional Flow Router)
docs.text: The Gate node acts as a switchable valve in your dataflow pipeline. It enables or stops data propagation along a branch without deleting or rewiring connections.

docs.title: Key Rules
docs.text:
• Single Input, Multiple Outputs: The In terminal accepts only 1 incoming connection to prevent collisions. The Out terminal supports multiple connections (fan-out).
  • Dynamic IOType: The gate starts as IOTypes.ANY and automatically adapts to match connected wires. Hover over In or Out to see the current type.
  • Pass-Through Toggle: Toggle the Pass checkbox directly on the node (or right-click → Toggle Pass-through). When enabled, data passes through; when disabled, data is dropped.
  • Canvas Highlighting: In highlight mode, open gates let wire highlights pass through to downstream nodes. Closed gates block highlight propagation.

Gate States in Views

Gate pass-through states (ON / OFF) are automatically preserved when exporting a View and restored upon loading. See Views & Dynamic Flow Routing.

docs.title: Edit Module UI (Module Item Inspector)
docs.text:
The Module Item Inspector allows you to inspect, declutter, and customize the user interface of any module window by selectively hiding widgets (buttons, plots, inputs).

Open it by right-clicking any node on the canvas and selecting Edit Module.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Widget Hierarchy Tree: Displays the full UI arborescence of the module. Toggle the checkbox next to any item to show or hide it.
  • Live Hover Highlighting: Hovering over an item in the tree draws a bounding overlay around that widget on the live window.
  • Interactive Pick Mode: Click Pick Element, hover over any widget on the module window, and click to automatically locate and highlight it in the tree.
  • Search & Reset: Filter widgets by tag/label using the search bar, or click Show All Elements to restore full visibility.
  • View & Flow Persistence: Hidden widget states (hidden_items) are automatically preserved when exporting Views or saving pipeline JSON files, and restored upon loading.

docs.title: Node Editor Menu Bar
docs.text: Menu Item Shortcut Description Load Pipeline… Load a full workspace from a JSON file (replaces current canvas) Load Sub-pipeline… Append nodes and connections from a file without clearing current canvas Load Reload Last Sub-pipeline Quickly reload the last appended sub-pipeline file Load From Clipboard… Paste a serialized pipeline copied from the clipboard Save Edit / Update Pipeline… Surgically update node positions and connections in an existing JSON without altering views or metadata Save Pipeline to File… Export the entire workspace to a .json file Save Pipeline to Clipboard Copy the serialized workspace JSON to the clipboard Save Current View to Pipeline… Save current window positions and gate states into the pipeline Clear Delete Selected Del Delete selected nodes and links Clear Clear Selection Esc Deselect all currently selected nodes and links Clear Clear All Nodes Delete every node and link from the editor Views (Saved Views) Dynamically lists saved views to switch window layouts and Gate states in one click Highlight Show All / Closest / Selection / None Select downstream highlight propagation mode Profiling Profiling (Checkbox) Toggle real-time performance tracking (zero overhead when disabled) Profiling Show Heartbeat Pulse-color active nodes and links dynamically during live dataflow Profiling Pulse on Continuous Streams Animate heartbeat pulses on high-frequency streaming connections Profiling Show Virtual Links Display activity across virtual Link Out → Link In channels Profiling Heartbeat Hold Duration Set pulse duration (Fast 150ms, Normal 240ms, Slow 450ms) Profiling Reset All Node Metrics Reset all accumulated execution timestamps and statistics Profiling Close All Reports Close all open floating node performance telemetry report windows

docs.title: Flow File Format
docs.text:
Workspaces are stored as human-readable JSON:

{
    "is_relative": true,
    "windows": [
        {
            "uuid": "41680190-3cb8-4a57-b08f-287df5d1bf2b",
            "module": "modules.basic_ui.csv_reader_win",
            "pos": [15.2, 20.4],
            "size": [30.5, 40.0],
            "visible": true,
            "params": {
                "default_path": "data/samples.csv"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        {
            "from": "41680190-3cb8-4a57-b08f-287df5d1bf2b",
            "output": "CSV_DATA",
            "to": "50c3d9a4-2e91-4c17-910a-3cb7217fd8b2"
        }
    ],
    "link_nodes": [
        {
            "kind": "gate",
            "uuid": "7a8b9c0d-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678",
            "label": "Gate_Branch_B",
            "is_open": true,
            "io_type": "FRAME",
            "node_pos": [250, 180],
            "connections": {
                "Out": ["target-module-uuid"]
            },
            "incoming": {
                "source_uuid": "source-module-uuid",
                "output_key": "Frame"
            }
        }
    ]
}
Field Description is_relative If true, pos/size are screen percentages (portable across resolutions) uuid Unique identifier for the node instance module Python import path of the module class params Saved values from the module's persistent_fields list connections Wires between output terminals and destination nodes link_nodes Built-in proxy nodes (Link In, Link Out, Gate, Working Directory, and Propagation Tester)

docs.title: Views & Dynamic Flow Routing
docs.text: Views are named presets that save both window layouts (position, size, visibility of each module window) and Gate pass-through states (is_open).

docs.title: Dynamic Flow Routing via Views
docs.text:
Because Views store Gate states, you can dynamically alter the active routing of your pipeline simply by switching Views!

graph TD
    subgraph "Flow Architecture"
        Source["Camera Module A"] --> G1{"Gate 1"}
        Source --> G2{"Gate 2"}
        G1 --> ProcessB["Real-time Filter Module B"]
        G2 --> ProcessC["High-res Saver Module C"]
    end

    subgraph "In View A: Live Preview"
        G1_A["Gate 1: OPEN"] ==> ProcessB
        G2_A["Gate 2: BLOCKED"] -.-> ProcessC
    end

    subgraph "In View B: Recording Mode"
        G1_B["Gate 1: BLOCKED"] -.-> ProcessB
        G2_B["Gate 2: OPEN"] ==> ProcessC
    end
  • Export View: Save current window layout and live Gate states into a named preset via Main Window → Workspace → Export View... or from the Pipeline Editor.
  • Apply View: Switching views via the Views menu or programmatically via apply_named_view("ViewName") applies window positioning and toggles all Gates to their saved state.
  • Pipeline Editor: Under the Views tab, expand the Gates in this View section to individually toggle which gates are pass-through for the selected view.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Auto-generated API documentation from source code docstrings.

docs.title: WindowBase
docs.text:
Base class for GUI modules in the system. Handles window creation, merging, serialization, and connectivity between modules.

Source code in core\window_base.py 
class WindowBase:
    """
    Base class for GUI modules in the system.
    Handles window creation, merging, serialization, and connectivity between modules.
    """

    _batch_loading: bool = False

    label: str
    pos: Tuple[int, int]
    win_width: int
    win_height: int
    visible: bool
    outputs: Dict[str, Any]
    UUID: str
    winID: str
    handler_tag: Optional[Union[int, str]]
    accepted_input_types: List[Any]
    description: str
    connections: Dict[str, List[Any]]
    persistent_fields: List[str]
    persistent_fields: List[str]
    _original_children: List[Union[int, str]]
    merged_into: Optional[WindowBase]
    _merge_wrapper_id: Optional[Union[int, str]]

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str = "Window",
        pos: Tuple[int, int] = (50, 50),
        win_width: int = -1,
        win_height: int = -1,
        uuid: Optional[str] = None,
        outputs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        visible: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize a WindowBase instance.

        Args:
            label: Display label of the window.
            pos: Tuple for initial window position.
            win_width: Initial window width.
            win_height: Initial window height.
            uuid: Optional unique identifier.
            outputs: Dictionary of output types.
            visible: Whether the window is visible at creation.
            **kwargs: Additional persistent fields to apply.
        """
        cls = type(self)

        # 1. Label resolution (argument -> class attribute -> EXPORTED_NAME -> "Window")
        if label != "Window":
            self.label = label
        elif hasattr(cls, "label") and cls.label != "Window":
            self.label = cls.label
        elif hasattr(cls, "EXPORTED_NAME") and cls.EXPORTED_NAME:
            self.label = cls.EXPORTED_NAME
        else:
            self.label = "Window"

        # 2. Geometry & Visibility (argument -> class attribute -> default)
        self.win_width = win_width if win_width != -1 else getattr(cls, "win_width", -1)
        self.win_height = win_height if win_height != -1 else getattr(cls, "win_height", -1)
        self.pos = pos if pos != (50, 50) else getattr(cls, "pos", (50, 50))
        self.visible = visible if visible is not True else getattr(cls, "visible", True)

        self.UUID = uuid or str(dpg.generate_uuid())
        self.winID = f"{self.label}_{self.UUID}"
        self.handler_tag = None
        self.description = ""

        if outputs is not None:
            self.outputs = outputs
        elif not hasattr(self, "outputs"):
            self.outputs = {}
        else:
            self.outputs = dict(self.outputs)

        if not hasattr(self, "accepted_input_types"):
            self.accepted_input_types = []
        else:
            self.accepted_input_types = list(self.accepted_input_types)

        # Resolve persistent fields (persistent_fields -> persistent_fields -> ["label"])
        raw_fields = getattr(self, "persistent_fields", getattr(self, "persistent_fields", None))
        if raw_fields is None:
            raw_fields = getattr(cls, "persistent_fields", getattr(cls, "persistent_fields", ["label"]))

        self.persistent_fields = list(raw_fields)
        if "label" not in self.persistent_fields:
            self.persistent_fields.insert(0, "label")
        self.persistent_fields = self.persistent_fields

        for field in self.persistent_fields:
            if field in kwargs:
                setattr(self, field, kwargs[field])
            elif hasattr(cls, field):
                setattr(self, field, getattr(cls, field))
            elif not hasattr(self, field):
                setattr(self, field, None)

        if not hasattr(self, "connections"):
            self.connections = {k: [] for k in self.outputs}
        self._original_children = []
        self.merged_into = None
        self._merge_wrapper_id = None

        register_module(self)

    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Intercept attribute assignments to auto-synchronize connections and persistent fields."""
        super().__setattr__(name, value)
        if name == "outputs" and isinstance(value, dict):
            conns = getattr(self, "connections", None)
            if conns is None:
                super().__setattr__("connections", {k: [] for k in value})
            else:
                for k in value:
                    if k not in conns:
                        conns[k] = []
        elif name == "persistent_fields":
            super().__setattr__("persistent_fields", value)
        elif name == "persistent_fields":
            super().__setattr__("persistent_fields", value)

    def update_permission(self) -> None:
        """
        Adjust module permissions and UI visibility based on app_state.mode.
        Subclasses should override this to hide/show or lock specific widgets.
        """
        pass

    def window(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """
        Convenience context manager to create the DPG window with this module's standard settings.
        Usage:
            with self.window():
                dpg.add_button(...)
        """
        params = {
            "label": self.label,
            "width": self.win_width,
            "height": self.win_height,
            "pos": self.pos,
            "tag": self.winID,
            "show": self.visible,
        }
        params.update(kwargs)
        return dpg.window(**params)

    def _list_children(self) -> List[Union[int, str]]:
        """Save the current list of children for potential restoration."""
        if dpg.does_item_exist(self.winID):
            return dpg.get_item_children(self.winID, 1) or []
        return []

    def inform_leaving(self, child_id: List[Union[int, str]]) -> None:
        """Notify the target window that this window is leaving (used in recursive merges)."""
        for child in child_id:
            if child in self._original_children:
                self._original_children.remove(child)

        if self.merged_into is not None:
            self.merged_into.inform_leaving(child_id)

    def merge_into(self, target_window: WindowBase) -> None:
        """
        Move all widgets into another WindowBase instance.
        Restore first if already merged.
        """
        if not isinstance(target_window, WindowBase):
            raise TypeError("target_window must be a WindowBase")

        if self.merged_into is target_window:
            return

        if self.merged_into is not None:
            self.restore_contents()

        childrens = self._list_children()

        if set(childrens) & set(target_window._original_children):
            logger.warning(f"Cannot merge {self.label} into {target_window.label}: cyclic merge detected.")
            return

        self._original_children = childrens

        src_height = 300
        if dpg.does_item_exist(self.winID):
            sz = dpg.get_item_rect_size(self.winID)
            if sz and sz[1] > 50:
                src_height = int(sz[1])

        self._merge_wrapper_id = dpg.generate_uuid()
        with dpg.child_window(
            border=True,
            autosize_x=True,
            height=src_height,
            tag=self._merge_wrapper_id,
            parent=target_window.winID,
        ):
            pass

        for child in self._original_children:
            dpg.move_item(child, parent=self._merge_wrapper_id)

        dpg.hide_item(self.winID)
        self.merged_into = target_window

    def restore_contents(self) -> None:
        """Move back previously moved widgets to this window and remove the wrapper."""
        if self.merged_into is None:
            logger.warning(f"Cannot restore {self.label}: not merged into any window.")
            return

        self.merged_into.inform_leaving(self._original_children)
        for child in self._original_children:
            if dpg.does_item_exist(child):
                dpg.move_item(child, parent=self.winID)

        if self._merge_wrapper_id and dpg.does_item_exist(self._merge_wrapper_id):
            dpg.delete_item(self._merge_wrapper_id)
        self._merge_wrapper_id = None

        self._original_children.clear()
        self.merged_into = None
        dpg.show_item(self.winID)

    def is_merged(self) -> bool:
        """Check whether this window has been merged elsewhere."""
        return bool(self._original_children)

    def absorb(self, source_window: WindowBase) -> None:
        """Merge another window's content into this one."""
        if not isinstance(source_window, WindowBase):
            raise TypeError("source_window must be a WindowBase")
        source_window.merge_into(self)

    def eject(self, absorbed_window: WindowBase) -> None:
        """Restore a previously absorbed window."""
        if not isinstance(absorbed_window, WindowBase):
            raise TypeError("eject() expects a WindowBase instance.")
        absorbed_window.restore_contents()

    def get_merge_target_label(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Returns the label of the window this one is merged into, or None."""
        return self.merged_into.label if self.merged_into else None

    def connect_to(self, target: Any, output: Optional[Union[str, int]] = None) -> bool:
        """
        Connect this module to another based on output type compatibility.

        Args:
            target: The target WindowBase instance.
            output: Output name (str) or index (int).

        Returns:
            True if the connection is valid and made, False otherwise.
        """
        from core.input_output_types import IOTypes

        if not hasattr(target, "accepted_input_types"):
            logger.error(f"Target {target} has no accepted_input_types")
            return False

        if isinstance(output, int):
            try:
                output_key = list(self.outputs.keys())[output]
            except IndexError:
                logger.error(f"Invalid output index: {output}")
                return False
        elif isinstance(output, str):
            if output not in self.outputs:
                logger.error(f"Output key '{output}' not found in outputs")
                return False
            output_key = output
        else:
            logger.error(f"Output must be a key (str) or index (int), got {type(output)}")
            return False

        output_type = self.outputs[output_key]
        input_types = getattr(target, "accepted_input_types", [])

        is_compatible = (
            not input_types
            or output_type == IOTypes.ANY
            or IOTypes.ANY in input_types
            or output_type in input_types
        )

        if not is_compatible:
            logger.warning(f"Incompatible types: {output_type} -> {input_types}")
            return False

        if output_key not in self.connections:
            self.connections[output_key] = []

        if target not in self.connections[output_key]:
            self.connections[output_key].append(target)

        return True

    def _is_output_compatible_with(self, target: Any) -> bool:
        """Internal: Check if any output type is compatible with target's accepted input types."""
        from core.input_output_types import IOTypes

        input_types = getattr(target, "accepted_input_types", [])
        if not input_types or IOTypes.ANY in input_types:
            return True

        for o in self.outputs.values():
            if o == IOTypes.ANY or o in input_types:
                return True
        return False

    def disconnect_from(self, *windows: WindowBase) -> None:
        """Disconnect this module from the provided windows."""
        for win in windows:
            for targets in self.connections.values():
                while win in targets:
                    targets.remove(win)


    def serialize(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize window state and configuration for saving/restoration."""
        if dpg.does_item_exist(self.winID):
            self.pos = dpg.get_item_pos(self.winID)
            self.win_width, self.win_height = dpg.get_item_rect_size(self.winID)
            self.visible = dpg.is_item_visible(self.winID)

        fields = getattr(self, "persistent_fields", getattr(self, "persistent_fields", ["label"]))
        params = {field: getattr(self, field, None) for field in fields if hasattr(self, field)}

        if self.merged_into:
            params["merged_into"] = self.merged_into.UUID

        res = {
            "module": self.__class__.__module__.replace("modules.", ""),
            "class_name": self.__class__.__name__,
            "uuid": self.UUID,
            "pos": self.pos,
            "size": [self.win_width, self.win_height],
            "visible": self.visible,
            "params": params,
        }

        try:
            from core.module_item_inspector import ModuleItemInspector
            hidden = ModuleItemInspector.get_hidden_items(self)
            if hidden:
                res["hidden_items"] = hidden
        except Exception:
            pass

        return res

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Clean up and unregister the window from the registry."""
        if getattr(self, "_is_closed", False):
            return
        self._is_closed = True
        self._is_closing = True

        logger.trace(f"Closing {self.label} ({self.UUID})")
        if hasattr(self, "on_close") and callable(self.on_close):
            try:
                self.on_close()
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Error during on_close of {self.label}: {e}")

        tags_to_delete = set()
        uuid_str = str(self.UUID)

        for attr_name, val in list(self.__dict__.items()):
            def check_and_add(tag: Any) -> None:
                if isinstance(tag, str) and uuid_str in tag:
                    tags_to_delete.add(tag)

            if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):
                for item in val:
                    check_and_add(item)
            elif isinstance(val, dict):
                for k, v in val.items():
                    check_and_add(k)
                    check_and_add(v)
            else:
                check_and_add(val)

        try:
            for item in dpg.get_all_items():
                if isinstance(item, str):
                    if uuid_str in item:
                        tags_to_delete.add(item)
                else:
                    alias = dpg.get_item_alias(item)
                    if alias and uuid_str in alias:
                        tags_to_delete.add(item)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to scan DPG items for UUID {self.UUID}: {e}")

        if dpg.does_item_exist(self.winID):
            try:
                dpg.delete_item(self.winID)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to delete winID {self.winID}: {e}")

        sub_windows = getattr(self, "sub_windows", [])
        for sub_win in sub_windows:
            try:
                if dpg.does_item_exist(sub_win):
                    dpg.delete_item(sub_win)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to delete sub_win {sub_win}: {e}")

        if hasattr(self, "handler_tag") and self.handler_tag:
            try:
                if dpg.does_item_exist(self.handler_tag):
                    dpg.delete_item(self.handler_tag)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to delete handler_tag {self.handler_tag}: {e}")

        for tag in tags_to_delete:
            try:
                if dpg.does_item_exist(tag):
                    dpg.delete_item(tag)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to delete tag {tag}: {e}")

        unregister_module(self)
        self.connections.clear()

    def on_close(self) -> None:
        """Stub method for subclasses to override for custom cleanup logic."""
        pass

    def __del__(self) -> None:
        if logger is not None:
            label = getattr(self, "label", "Unknown")
            uuid = getattr(self, "UUID", "Unknown")
            logger.info(f"WindowBase {label} ({uuid}) has been deleted.")

    def is_outputs_ready(self) -> bool:
        """Check if all connected targets are ready to receive data."""
        for modules in self.connections.values():
            for module in modules:
                is_ready = getattr(module, "is_ready", lambda: True)
                if callable(is_ready) and not is_ready():
                    return False
        return True

    def autosize_window(self, winID: Optional[Union[int, str]] = None) -> None:
        """Triggers a one-shot autosize to fit window content."""
        if WindowBase._batch_loading:
            return
        if winID is None:
            winID = self.winID
        if dpg.does_item_exist(winID):
            dpg.configure_item(winID, autosize=True)
            dpg.split_frame()
            dpg.configure_item(winID, autosize=False)

def __init__(
    self,
    label: str = "Window",
    pos: Tuple[int, int] = (50, 50),
    win_width: int = -1,
    win_height: int = -1,
    uuid: Optional[str] = None,
    outputs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    visible: bool = True,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> None:
    """
    Initialize a WindowBase instance.

    Args:
        label: Display label of the window.
        pos: Tuple for initial window position.
        win_width: Initial window width.
        win_height: Initial window height.
        uuid: Optional unique identifier.
        outputs: Dictionary of output types.
        visible: Whether the window is visible at creation.
        **kwargs: Additional persistent fields to apply.
    """
    cls = type(self)

    # 1. Label resolution (argument -> class attribute -> EXPORTED_NAME -> "Window")
    if label != "Window":
        self.label = label
    elif hasattr(cls, "label") and cls.label != "Window":
        self.label = cls.label
    elif hasattr(cls, "EXPORTED_NAME") and cls.EXPORTED_NAME:
        self.label = cls.EXPORTED_NAME
    else:
        self.label = "Window"

    # 2. Geometry & Visibility (argument -> class attribute -> default)
    self.win_width = win_width if win_width != -1 else getattr(cls, "win_width", -1)
    self.win_height = win_height if win_height != -1 else getattr(cls, "win_height", -1)
    self.pos = pos if pos != (50, 50) else getattr(cls, "pos", (50, 50))
    self.visible = visible if visible is not True else getattr(cls, "visible", True)

    self.UUID = uuid or str(dpg.generate_uuid())
    self.winID = f"{self.label}_{self.UUID}"
    self.handler_tag = None
    self.description = ""

    if outputs is not None:
        self.outputs = outputs
    elif not hasattr(self, "outputs"):
        self.outputs = {}
    else:
        self.outputs = dict(self.outputs)

    if not hasattr(self, "accepted_input_types"):
        self.accepted_input_types = []
    else:
        self.accepted_input_types = list(self.accepted_input_types)

    # Resolve persistent fields (persistent_fields -> persistent_fields -> ["label"])
    raw_fields = getattr(self, "persistent_fields", getattr(self, "persistent_fields", None))
    if raw_fields is None:
        raw_fields = getattr(cls, "persistent_fields", getattr(cls, "persistent_fields", ["label"]))

    self.persistent_fields = list(raw_fields)
    if "label" not in self.persistent_fields:
        self.persistent_fields.insert(0, "label")
    self.persistent_fields = self.persistent_fields

    for field in self.persistent_fields:
        if field in kwargs:
            setattr(self, field, kwargs[field])
        elif hasattr(cls, field):
            setattr(self, field, getattr(cls, field))
        elif not hasattr(self, field):
            setattr(self, field, None)

    if not hasattr(self, "connections"):
        self.connections = {k: [] for k in self.outputs}
    self._original_children = []
    self.merged_into = None
    self._merge_wrapper_id = None

    register_module(self)

def connect_to(self, target: Any, output: Optional[Union[str, int]] = None) -> bool:
    """
    Connect this module to another based on output type compatibility.

    Args:
        target: The target WindowBase instance.
        output: Output name (str) or index (int).

    Returns:
        True if the connection is valid and made, False otherwise.
    """
    from core.input_output_types import IOTypes

    if not hasattr(target, "accepted_input_types"):
        logger.error(f"Target {target} has no accepted_input_types")
        return False

    if isinstance(output, int):
        try:
            output_key = list(self.outputs.keys())[output]
        except IndexError:
            logger.error(f"Invalid output index: {output}")
            return False
    elif isinstance(output, str):
        if output not in self.outputs:
            logger.error(f"Output key '{output}' not found in outputs")
            return False
        output_key = output
    else:
        logger.error(f"Output must be a key (str) or index (int), got {type(output)}")
        return False

    output_type = self.outputs[output_key]
    input_types = getattr(target, "accepted_input_types", [])

    is_compatible = (
        not input_types
        or output_type == IOTypes.ANY
        or IOTypes.ANY in input_types
        or output_type in input_types
    )

    if not is_compatible:
        logger.warning(f"Incompatible types: {output_type} -> {input_types}")
        return False

    if output_key not in self.connections:
        self.connections[output_key] = []

    if target not in self.connections[output_key]:
        self.connections[output_key].append(target)

    return True

def merge_into(self, target_window: WindowBase) -> None:
    """
    Move all widgets into another WindowBase instance.
    Restore first if already merged.
    """
    if not isinstance(target_window, WindowBase):
        raise TypeError("target_window must be a WindowBase")

    if self.merged_into is target_window:
        return

    if self.merged_into is not None:
        self.restore_contents()

    childrens = self._list_children()

    if set(childrens) & set(target_window._original_children):
        logger.warning(f"Cannot merge {self.label} into {target_window.label}: cyclic merge detected.")
        return

    self._original_children = childrens

    src_height = 300
    if dpg.does_item_exist(self.winID):
        sz = dpg.get_item_rect_size(self.winID)
        if sz and sz[1] > 50:
            src_height = int(sz[1])

    self._merge_wrapper_id = dpg.generate_uuid()
    with dpg.child_window(
        border=True,
        autosize_x=True,
        height=src_height,
        tag=self._merge_wrapper_id,
        parent=target_window.winID,
    ):
        pass

    for child in self._original_children:
        dpg.move_item(child, parent=self._merge_wrapper_id)

    dpg.hide_item(self.winID)
    self.merged_into = target_window

def restore_contents(self) -> None:
    """Move back previously moved widgets to this window and remove the wrapper."""
    if self.merged_into is None:
        logger.warning(f"Cannot restore {self.label}: not merged into any window.")
        return

    self.merged_into.inform_leaving(self._original_children)
    for child in self._original_children:
        if dpg.does_item_exist(child):
            dpg.move_item(child, parent=self.winID)

    if self._merge_wrapper_id and dpg.does_item_exist(self._merge_wrapper_id):
        dpg.delete_item(self._merge_wrapper_id)
    self._merge_wrapper_id = None

    self._original_children.clear()

    dpg.show_item(self.winID)

docs.title: ProcessingBase
docs.text:
Base class for multiprocessing-based data processing modules.

This class manages a background worker process that receives data via an input queue, processes it using a subclass-defined _process_data() method, and returns the result via an output queue.

Drop policies
  • 'drop_new': when the input queue is full, the incoming item is rejected (cheap, producer side).
  • 'block': when the input queue is full, the producer blocks until space is available.
  • 'drop_oldest': "latest wins". Implemented on the WORKER side: a receiver thread inside the worker process continuously drains the IPC queue into a local bounded buffer and discards the oldest items. The producer never has to read (unpickle) frames back from the pipe just to throw them away, which used to stall the main process.

Supports runtime parameter updates and runtime drop-policy changes (set_drop_policy).

Shared-memory transport (transparent): Large numpy arrays found in submitted data or in results (directly, or inside tuple / list / dict) are passed through reusable shared-memory slots instead of being pickled through the pipe (see core/shm_transport.py). Subclasses keep receiving / returning ordinary numpy arrays. Tunables (class attributes): use_shared_memory, shm_threshold_bytes, shm_max_pool_bytes.

class ProcessingBase:
    """
    Base class for multiprocessing-based data processing modules.

    This class manages a background worker process that receives data via an input queue,
    processes it using a subclass-defined `_process_data()` method, and returns the result
    via an output queue.

    Drop policies:
        - 'drop_new':    when the input queue is full, the incoming item is rejected (cheap, producer side).
        - 'block':       when the input queue is full, the producer blocks until space is available.
        - 'drop_oldest': "latest wins". Implemented on the WORKER side: a receiver thread inside the
                         worker process continuously drains the IPC queue into a local bounded buffer and
                         discards the oldest items. The producer never has to read (unpickle) frames back
                         from the pipe just to throw them away, which used to stall the main process.

    Supports runtime parameter updates and runtime drop-policy changes (`set_drop_policy`).

    Shared-memory transport (transparent):
        Large numpy arrays found in submitted data or in results (directly, or inside tuple / list / dict)
        are passed through reusable shared-memory slots instead of being pickled through the pipe
        (see core/shm_transport.py). Subclasses keep receiving / returning ordinary numpy arrays.
        Tunables (class attributes): `use_shared_memory`, `shm_threshold_bytes`, `shm_max_pool_bytes`.
    """
    buffer_size: int = 10
    drop_policy: str = "drop_new"
    daemon: bool = True

    use_shared_memory: bool = True
    shm_threshold_bytes: int = 64 * 1024  # arrays smaller than this keep the regular pickle path
    shm_max_pool_bytes: int = 512 * 1024 * 1024  # per direction cap; beyond it -> pickle fallback

    def __init__(
        self,
        params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        *,
        buffer_size: Optional[int] = None,
        out_buffer_size: Optional[int] = None,
        drop_policy: Optional[str] = None,
        daemon: Optional[bool] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the processing base.

        Args:
            params: Initial parameters dictionary passed to the worker.
            buffer_size: Max number of items in the input queue (arg -> class attribute -> 10).
            out_buffer_size: Max number of items in the output queue (arg -> class attribute -> buffer_size if block else 1).
            drop_policy: 'drop_new', 'drop_oldest', or 'block' (arg -> class attribute -> 'drop_new').
            daemon: Whether the worker process runs as a daemon (arg -> class attribute -> True).
            **kwargs: Extra arguments forwarded safely.
        """
        cls = type(self)
        self.params: Dict[str, Any] = dict(params) if params else {}
        self._drop_policy = (
            drop_policy if drop_policy is not None else getattr(cls, "drop_policy", "drop_new")
        )
        resolved_buffer_size = (
            buffer_size if buffer_size is not None else getattr(cls, "buffer_size", 10)
        )
        self._buffer_size: int = max(1, int(resolved_buffer_size))
        out_buf = out_buffer_size if out_buffer_size is not None else getattr(cls, "out_buffer_size", None)
        if out_buf is not None:
            self._out_buffer_size: int = max(1, int(out_buf))
        else:
            self._out_buffer_size = self._buffer_size if self._drop_policy == "block" else 1

        self._daemon = daemon if daemon is not None else getattr(cls, "daemon", True)

        self._in_queue: mp.Queue[Any] = mp.Queue(maxsize=self._buffer_size)
        self._out_queue: mp.Queue[Any] = mp.Queue(maxsize=self._out_buffer_size)
        self._ctrl_queue: mp.Queue[Tuple[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]] = mp.Queue()

        # Shared counters (written by the worker, read by the main process)
        self._worker_dropped = mp.Value("q", 0)  # items discarded by the worker-side drop_oldest buffer
        self._worker_pending = mp.Value("i", 0, lock=False)  # items waiting in the worker-side local buffer

        # Transparent shared-memory transport for large numpy arrays (one pool per direction)
        self._in_pool: Optional[ShmPool] = None
        self._out_pool: Optional[ShmPool] = None
        if SHM_AVAILABLE and bool(getattr(cls, "use_shared_memory", True)):
            try:
                threshold = int(getattr(cls, "shm_threshold_bytes", 64 * 1024))
                cap = int(getattr(cls, "shm_max_pool_bytes", 512 * 1024 * 1024))
                # In flight: IPC queue + worker-side buffer + 1 being decoded, up to 2 arrays per item.
                self._in_pool = ShmPool(min(128, 2 * (2 * self._buffer_size + 2)), threshold, cap)
                out_slots = min(128, max(8, 2 * (self._out_buffer_size + 2)))
                self._out_pool = ShmPool(out_slots, threshold, cap)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Shared-memory transport disabled: {e}")
                self._in_pool = None
                self._out_pool = None

        self._process: Optional[mp.Process] = None

    def __getstate__(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Custom pickling state: strip unpicklable process handles and dynamically wrapped methods."""
        state = self.__dict__.copy()
        state.pop("submit", None)
        state.pop("_perf_orig_submit", None)
        state["_process"] = None
        return state

    def __setstate__(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Restore state in child process."""
        self.__dict__.update(state)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Main-process API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def start(self) -> None:
        """Start or restart the worker process."""
        if self._process and self._process.is_alive():
            return
        self._process = mp.Process(target=self._worker_entrypoint, daemon=self._daemon)
        self._process.start()

    def stop(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Request the worker to stop and wait for graceful shutdown."""
        if not self._process or not self._process.is_alive():
            return
        self._ctrl_queue.put(("stop", None))
        self._process.join(timeout)
        if self._process.is_alive():
            logger.warning("Worker did not stop gracefully, terminating...")
            self._process.terminate()
        self._process = None
        # Items still pending in in_queue will never be read: don't let the feeder thread block the
        # main process at interpreter exit while trying to flush them into the pipe.
        try:
            self._in_queue.cancel_join_thread()
        except Exception:
            pass
        # Worker is gone: no shared-memory slot can be in use anymore.
        for q in (self._in_queue, self._out_queue):
            try:
                while True:
                    q.get_nowait()
            except Exception:
                pass
        for pool in (self._in_pool, self._out_pool):
            if pool is not None:
                pool.close()
                pool.reset()

    # -- shared-memory helpers (no-ops when the transport is disabled) --
    def _encode_in(self, data: Any) -> Any:
        pool = self._in_pool
        return pool.encode(data) if pool is not None else data

    def _release_in(self, item: Any) -> None:
        if self._in_pool is not None:
            self._in_pool.release_item(item)

    def _release_out(self, item: Any) -> None:
        if self._out_pool is not None:
            self._out_pool.release_item(item)

    def is_ready(self) -> bool:
        """Check if worker is alive and queues (IPC + worker-side buffer) are not saturated."""
        if not (self._process and self._process.is_alive()):
            return False
        if self._out_queue.full():
            return False
        size = self.queue_size()
        if size < 0:  # qsize() unsupported on this platform
            return not self._in_queue.full()
        return size < self._buffer_size

    def submit(self, data: Any, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> bool:
        """
        Try to submit data to the worker for processing.

        Args:
            data: Input to be processed.
            timeout: Timeout if blocking is used (drop_policy='block').

        Returns:
            True if data was successfully submitted, False otherwise.
        """
        policy = self._drop_policy
        # Cheap pre-check: don't copy a frame into shared memory just to reject it right after.
        if policy != "block":
            try:
                if self._in_queue.full():
                    return False
            except Exception:
                pass

        item = self._encode_in(data)
        try:
            self._in_queue.put_nowait(item)
            return True
        except queue.Full:
            if policy == "block":
                try:
                    self._in_queue.put(item, timeout=timeout)
                    return True
                except queue.Full:
                    self._release_in(item)
                    return False
            elif policy in ("drop_oldest", "drop_new"):
                # drop_oldest: the worker's receiver thread keeps the IPC queue drained, so a full IPC
                # queue means the worker cannot even keep up with receiving. Reject the item instead of
                # reading a stale one back from the pipe in the producer process (very expensive).
                self._release_in(item)
                return False
            else:
                self._release_in(item)
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid drop_policy: {policy}")
        except BaseException:
            self._release_in(item)
            raise

    def set_drop_policy(self, policy: str) -> None:
        """Change the drop policy at runtime (applied on both producer and worker side)."""
        if policy not in _VALID_POLICIES:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid drop_policy: {policy}")
        self._drop_policy = policy
        try:
            self._ctrl_queue.put(("policy", {"drop_policy": policy}))
        except Exception:
            pass

    def get(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[Any]:
        """
        Get the next processed result from the output queue.

        Args:
            timeout: None or <= 0 -> non-blocking (returns None immediately if empty).
                     > 0 -> block up to `timeout` seconds. Blocking releases the GIL and wakes up
                     exactly when a result arrives (preferred over get() + sleep() polling loops).

        Returns:
            The processed result or None if no result is available.
        """
        try:
            if timeout is None or timeout <= 0:
                item = self._out_queue.get_nowait()
            else:
                item = self._out_queue.get(timeout=timeout)
        except queue.Empty:
            return None
        except (EOFError, OSError):
            return None
        pool = self._out_pool
        return pool.decode(item) if pool is not None else item

    # Alias to match documentation and hybrid node patterns
    poll_result = get
    get_results = get

    def has_data(self) -> bool:
        """Check if output queue has at least one processed result ready."""
        try:
            return not self._out_queue.empty()
        except Exception:
            return False

    def queue_size(self) -> int:
        """
        Get the current number of pending items (IPC input queue + worker-side buffer).

        Returns:
            Number of pending items or -1 if unsupported.
        """
        try:
            ipc = self._in_queue.qsize()
        except NotImplementedError:
            return -1
        return ipc + max(0, int(self._worker_pending.value))

    def drop_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of items discarded inside the worker by the drop_oldest policy."""
        try:
            return int(self._worker_dropped.value)
        except Exception:
            return 0

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear all pending items in in_queue and out_queue."""
        while not self._in_queue.empty():
            try:
                self._release_in(self._in_queue.get_nowait())
            except (queue.Empty, Exception):
                break
        while not self._out_queue.empty():
            try:
                self._release_out(self._out_queue.get_nowait())
            except (queue.Empty, Exception):
                break
        try:
            self._ctrl_queue.put_nowait(("clear", None))
        except Exception:
            pass

    def update_params(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """
        Send a parameter update command to the worker process.

        Args:
            kwargs: Key-value pairs to update.
        """
        self._ctrl_queue.put(("update", kwargs))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Worker-process internals
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _drain_ctrl_queue(self) -> bool:
        """Apply all pending control commands (worker side). Returns True if a stop was requested."""
        try:
            while True:
                cmd, payload = self._ctrl_queue.get_nowait()
                if cmd == "stop":
                    return True
                elif cmd == "update" and payload:
                    self.params.update(payload)
                elif cmd == "policy" and payload:
                    self._drop_policy = payload.get("drop_policy", self._drop_policy)
                elif cmd == "clear":
                    self._clear_local_buffer()
                    while not self._in_queue.empty():
                        try:
                            self._release_in(self._in_queue.get_nowait())
                        except (queue.Empty, Exception):
                            break
        except (queue.Empty, Exception):
            pass
        return False

    def _init_worker_state(self) -> None:
        """Create worker-only objects (threads, locks, local buffer). Never pickled."""
        self._local_buf: Deque[Any] = collections.deque()
        self._local_cv = threading.Condition()
        self._receiver_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None

    def _ensure_receiver(self) -> None:
        """Start the drop_oldest receiver thread if needed (worker side)."""
        t = self._receiver_thread
        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
            return
        self._receiver_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._receiver_loop, name="ProcessingBase_receiver", daemon=True
        )
        self._receiver_thread.start()

    def _receiver_loop(self) -> None:
        """
        Worker-side receiver for drop_oldest: drains the IPC queue as fast as possible into a local
        bounded buffer, discarding the oldest items. Exits when the policy changes.
        """
        while self._drop_policy == "drop_oldest":
            try:
                item = self._in_queue.get(timeout=0.05)
            except queue.Empty:
                continue
            except (EOFError, OSError):
                return
            with self._local_cv:
                while len(self._local_buf) >= self._buffer_size:
                    # Discarded without decoding: just free its shared-memory slots.
                    self._release_in(self._local_buf.popleft())
                    with self._worker_dropped.get_lock():
                        self._worker_dropped.value += 1
                self._local_buf.append(item)
                self._worker_pending.value = len(self._local_buf)
                self._local_cv.notify()

    def _clear_local_buffer(self) -> None:
        cv = getattr(self, "_local_cv", None)
        if cv is None:
            return
        with cv:
            for item in self._local_buf:
                self._release_in(item)
            self._local_buf.clear()
            self._worker_pending.value = 0

    def _next_item(self, timeout: float) -> Any:
        """Fetch the next item to process (worker side). Raises queue.Empty on timeout."""
        # Items already buffered locally are always served first (also after a policy switch).
        with self._local_cv:
            if self._drop_policy == "drop_oldest":
                self._ensure_receiver()
                if not self._local_buf:
                    self._local_cv.wait(timeout)
            if self._local_buf:
                item = self._local_buf.popleft()
                self._worker_pending.value = len(self._local_buf)
                return item
            if self._drop_policy == "drop_oldest":
                raise queue.Empty
        return self._in_queue.get(timeout=timeout)

    def _worker_entrypoint(self) -> None:
        """
        Internal method run by the worker process.
        Listens for control commands and data to process.
        """
        self._init_worker_state()
        try:
            self._worker_loop()
        finally:
            # A result still buffered in the out_queue feeder (nobody reads it anymore) would make the
            # process hang at exit while flushing the pipe -> "did not stop gracefully" + terminate().
            try:
                self._out_queue.cancel_join_thread()
            except Exception:
                pass
            for pool in (self._in_pool, self._out_pool):
                if pool is not None:
                    pool.close()

    def _publish_result(self, result: Any) -> None:
        """Push a result to the out_queue, replacing a stale unread one if drop_policy is not 'block'."""
        item = self._out_pool.encode(result) if self._out_pool is not None else result
        try:
            self._out_queue.put_nowait(item)
            return
        except queue.Full:
            pass
        except Exception:
            self._release_out(item)
            return

        # In lossless 'block' mode, never discard completed results; block until out_queue is read
        if self._drop_policy == "block":
            try:
                self._out_queue.put(item)
                return
            except Exception:
                self._release_out(item)
                return

        # Lossy modes (drop_oldest / drop_new): replace stale unread result
        try:
            self._release_out(self._out_queue.get_nowait())
        except (queue.Empty, Exception):
            pass
        try:
            self._out_queue.put_nowait(item)
        except (queue.Full, Exception):
            self._release_out(item)

    def _worker_loop(self) -> None:
        while True:
            if self._drain_ctrl_queue():
                return

            try:
                item = self._next_item(timeout=0.01)
            except queue.Empty:
                continue
            except (EOFError, OSError):
                return

            # Params updates sent right before this item was submitted may not have been read yet
            # (the worker was blocked on the input queue): apply them before processing.
            if self._drain_ctrl_queue():
                self._release_in(item)
                return

            try:
                data = self._in_pool.decode(item) if self._in_pool is not None else item
                result = self._process_data(data, self.params)
                self._publish_result(result)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Error in worker: {e}")

    def _process_data(self, data: Any, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """
        Method to be overridden by subclasses to perform actual processing.

        Args:
            data: Input data to process.
            params: Current parameters dictionary.

        Returns:
            Processed output to be pushed to the output queue.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses must override _process_data()")

    self._process.join(timeout)
    if self._process.is_alive():
        logger.warning("Worker did not stop gracefully, terminating...")
        self._process.terminate()
    self._process = None
    # Items still pending in in_queue will never be read: don't let the feeder thread block the
    # main process at interpreter exit while trying to flush them into the pipe.
    try:
        self._in_queue.cancel_join_thread()
    except Exception:
        pass
    # Worker is gone: no shared-memory slot can be in use anymore.
    for q in (self._in_queue, self._out_queue):
        try:
            while True:
                q.get_nowait()
        except Exception:
            pass
    for pool in (self._in_pool, self._out_pool):
        if pool is not None:
            pool.close()
            pool.reset()

def submit(self, data: Any, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> bool:
    """
    Try to submit data to the worker for processing.

    Args:
        data: Input to be processed.
        timeout: Timeout if blocking is used (drop_policy='block').

    Returns:
        True if data was successfully submitted, False otherwise.
    """
    policy = self._drop_policy
    # Cheap pre-check: don't copy a frame into shared memory just to reject it right after.
    if policy != "block":
        try:
            if self._in_queue.full():
                return False
        except Exception:
            pass

    item = self._encode_in(data)
    try:
        self._in_queue.put_nowait(item)
        return True
    except queue.Full:
        if policy == "block":
            try:
                self._in_queue.put(item, timeout=timeout)
                return True
            except queue.Full:
                self._release_in(item)
                return False
        elif policy in ("drop_oldest", "drop_new"):
            # drop_oldest: the worker's receiver thread keeps the IPC queue drained, so a full IPC
            # queue means the worker cannot even keep up with receiving. Reject the item instead of
            # reading a stale one back from the pipe in the producer process (very expensive).
            self._release_in(item)
            return False
        else:
            self._release_in(item)
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid drop_policy: {policy}")
    except BaseException:
        self._release_in(item)
        raise
